name: lightroom-agent

tools.name: search_photos
tools.description: Search photos using intersecting Library filters (paginated): filename, keywords, rating, capture date, camera, lens, ISO, focal length, flag, color label, edited status, file type and folder. Provide at least one filter to improve performance on large catalogs. The hidden photos of a collapsed stack are not searched; a warning names the stack tops on the page. Rules: start_date and end_date must be real calendar dates; start_date must be on or before end_date.

include_path.description: Include each photo file path (default false). Rows always include photo_id, filename, rating (0 = unrated), flag, color_label and date_time_original, and stack (position, is_collapsed, top_photo_id) for a stacked photo.

camera.description: Exact camera name indexed by Lightroom

lens.description: Exact lens name indexed by Lightroom

focal_length.description: Exact focal length in millimeters (not the 35mm equivalent)

edited.description: Whether the photo has develop adjustments

file_type.description: Lightroom file format; camera raw formats use RAW

folder.description: Folder text, including parent folders shown in Lightroom's Folders panel (contains all words)

tools.name: get_selected_photos
tools.description: Get currently selected photos in Lightroom (or filmstrip if no selection). Paginated.

include_path.description: Include each photo file path (default false). Rows always include photo_id, filename, rating (0 = unrated), flag, color_label and date_time_original, and stack (position, is_collapsed, top_photo_id) for a stacked photo.

tools.name: get_photo_metadata
tools.description: Read 1-100 photos, field names in snake_case: rating (0 = unrated), flag and color_label in the set_rating_and_flag/set_color_label values, keywords/nested keyword_paths, EXIF, title/caption/headline, GPS latitude/longitude/altitude, IPTC sublocation/city/state_province/country/iso_country_code, copyright and accessibility alt_text/extended_description (omitted when empty); develop settings are read with get_develop_settings. photo_id and related ids are catalog-local strings. is_virtual_copy marks copies; optional virtual_copy holds master_photo_id and copy_name, or a master's copy_photo_ids. Optional folder stack holds position (top=1), is_collapsed, top_photo_id and ordered member_photo_ids.

photo_ids.description: 1 to 100 photo IDs or file paths; returns photos in request order; unknown identifiers are not_found. Repeated identifiers produce repeated entries.

tools.name: get_photo_preview
tools.description: Lightroom-rendered JPEG with Develop edits (raw supported). region crops the rendered frame after develop crop/rotation: normalized x/y/width/height, origin top-left, x right, y down. width/height/bytes are actual; requested_size is the edge asked of Lightroom; scaled_by_server is true when the server scaled Lightroom's larger image down. Lightroom sometimes answers that it has no preview pixels for a photo, typically right after a change; the call asks again for about 20 s and, if it still has none, fails with that reason: ask again later. Lightroom renders no preview of the photo open in Develop, so that photo is rendered from Library once running Develop operations finish: Lightroom switches to Library for about a second and back, restoring module, active photo, selection and source but not an open masking panel or the Develop tool. Lightroom's preview cache can answer with an enlargement of a smaller cached preview, most often on a cropped photo, without saying so; judge fine sharpness with get_photo_detail. See size for cost/edge rules. Rules: region must fit within the rendered frame (x + width and y + height at most 1).

size.description: Longest edge returned: cull is 864, review 1728, sizes Lightroom 16.0 renders itself for 3:2 raws, so they usually arrive without resampling; numeric 64-2048 means exactly that edge; default cull, the frequent call. The server scales a larger Lightroom image down to this edge, at most 2000px, within 3.5 MiB; a smaller image is returned as Lightroom made it. cull is for choosing among frames, review for a whole-frame look at rendering, tone and mask edges. Image tokens grow with pixel area (Claude: about width x height / 750) and repeat each turn in history.

region.description: Rectangle within the rendered preview, including its develop crop and displayed orientation. Pixel bounds round outward. Region calls request a larger source by dividing size by the longest normalized side, capped at 2048; requested_size reports that source request. A source over 2000px is scaled to 2000px before the crop; otherwise its pixels are cut as Lightroom rendered them.

tools.name: get_photo_detail
tools.description: Cut 1-4 regions from a full-resolution render of a photo with its current Develop settings, one rendered pixel per returned pixel, to judge sharpness of a detail such as the nearest eye. The render is a temporary export (JPEG quality 100, sRGB, output sharpening off, no catalog add), deleted before the call returns (one left by a timed-out or cancelled call, by a later detail call); it takes seconds, and a render that starts while another export or detail render runs is refused, not queued. Its first step reads the cropped frame and waits for the Develop calls before it, as every read of a photo's develop state does; the render runs alongside them. Each call adds one Export history step to the photo and marks it exported, so summarize_develop_settings' exported_only counts it; Develop settings and pixels stay unchanged, and no cached preview, selection or module changes. Returns photo_id, crop_jpeg_quality (95), per region its pixel box in the render and the image (JPEG 95), plus render {width, height, jpeg_quality, color_space, output_sharpening, source, left_on_photo}: source says how the render was made, a string ("export" today); left_on_photo says what the render left on the photo, a list of phrases ("one Export history step", "the exported mark"). A region larger than max_edge, measured against the cropped frame get_crop reports, is refused before the render with the largest normalized size this photo allows; nothing is scaled. A call refused before the render (unknown photo, the cropped frame not read, region over max_edge, export running) is failed with nothing left; an error once the render started is unknown and names the export and what it leaves on the photo. Rules: every region must fit within the rendered frame (x + width and y + height at most 1).

regions.description: Rectangles in the displayed frame after develop crop and rotation, normalized like get_photo_preview's region; pixel bounds round outward

max_edge.description: Largest region edge in pixels (default 1024). Keep it within what your model receives without downscaling; the server cannot know that limit.

tools.name: get_photo_previews
tools.description: Get JPEG thumbnails for 1–20 photos in input order for culling. Each preview names its photo_id and 1-based image_index, with width, height, bytes and scaled_by_server as in get_photo_preview; a photo that cannot be rendered is failed, the others still arrive; a photo Lightroom answers it has no preview pixels for is asked again within the time, which can leave the photos after it remaining. Lightroom renders no preview of the photo open in Develop, so that photo is rendered after the others, from Library once running Develop operations finish: Lightroom switches to Library for about a second and back, restoring module, active photo, selection and source but not an open masking panel or the Develop tool. Total budget 8 MiB. Photos not reached by 20 s or beyond the budget are remaining; resend them. Lightroom's preview cache can answer with an enlargement of a smaller cached preview, most often on a cropped photo, without saying so; judge fine sharpness with get_photo_detail. Catalog unchanged.

photo_ids.description: Between 1 and 20 IDs or paths, in image order

size.description: Longest edge returned: cull (864) or review (1728) as in get_photo_preview, or a number 64-2048; default 256. A larger Lightroom image is scaled down to it, at most 2000px

tools.name: find_duplicate_groups
tools.description: Group near-duplicates/bursts from up to 100 IDs/paths using 64-bit dHash of current JPEG previews (minimum edge 64) and raw capture time. Every pair must meet inclusive time_window_seconds (default 5) and max_hamming_distance (default 10). Input-order groups omit singletons and repeated photos. Similarity does not rank frames. photos gives raw capture_time in Lightroom seconds (second precision, no timezone normalization). No hash cache or catalog changes. At 20 s returns the groups so far and the unreached inputs as remaining; preview and missing-time failures are failed with reasons. Lightroom renders no preview of the photo open in Develop, so that photo is rendered after the others, from Library once running Develop operations finish: Lightroom switches to Library for about a second and back, restoring module, active photo, selection and source but not an open masking panel or the Develop tool. Resend remaining together with the originals to grow groups.

tools.name: get_photo_stats
tools.description: Measure current rendered JPEG previews for up to 20 photos; results by photo_id, failures as failed, photos not started within 20 s as remaining. histogram: 64 normalized Rec.709 luma bins (0-255, four levels/bin); mean_luminance same scale; shadow_fraction <=1, highlight_fraction >=254. sharpness: four-neighbor Laplacian variance after area resampling to 512px long edge (enlarges small previews); higher=sharper. These measure JPEG previews, not raw clipping/full-resolution focus. Lightroom renders no preview of the photo open in Develop, so that photo is rendered after the others, from Library once running Develop operations finish: Lightroom switches to Library for about a second and back, restoring module, active photo, selection and source but not an open masking panel or the Develop tool. Catalog unchanged.

photo_ids.description: Between 1 and 20 photo IDs or file paths, in result order

tools.name: set_gps
tools.description: Replace GPS coordinates in decimal degrees. Altitude stays unless altitude or clear_altitude is given. Returns updated (photos written); unknown IDs are not_found. Rules: altitude cannot be combined with clear_altitude.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

clear_altitude.description: Remove the photos' altitude (default false). Cannot be combined with altitude.

tools.name: set_location
tools.description: Set IPTC location fields from get_photo_metadata. Omitted fields stay, empty strings clear. GPS stays (use set_gps). Returns updated (photos written) and fields; unknown IDs are not_found. Rules: give at least one of sublocation, city, state_province, country, iso_country_code.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

sublocation.description: Sublocation: a venue, landmark or neighbourhood (e.g. 'Sydney Opera House')

tools.name: set_metadata
tools.description: Set IPTC text from get_photo_metadata. Omitted fields stay, empty strings clear. Copyright status is unwritable. Returns updated (photos written) and fields; unknown IDs are not_found. Rules: give at least one of title, caption, headline, creator, copyright, rights_usage_terms, copyright_info_url, creator_url, alt_text, extended_description.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

copyright_info_url.description: Copyright info URL, e.g. a licensing page

tools.name: set_ai_metadata
tools.description: Store an AI score and reason in private per-photo plug-in metadata in this catalog. Provide score, reason or both. Score is an integer from 0 to 100; reason is at most 1024 characters. Omitted fields stay unchanged; an empty string clears a field. Does not change IPTC, XMP, keywords, or export metadata. Returns updated (photos written); unknown IDs are not_found. Rules: give score or reason.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

tools.name: get_ai_metadata
tools.description: Read private per-photo AI scores and reasons in one batch (up to 1000 IDs or paths). Returns photos with photo_id, numeric score and reason, one per distinct photo; unset fields are omitted. Unknown IDs are not_found.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: List catalog folders in tree order as a paginated flat list of full paths, names and photo_count (direct photos only, excluding subfolders). Default limit 100.

tools.name: get_folder_photos
tools.description: List photos in a catalog folder by its full path from list_folders (paginated). Subfolders are excluded by default.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: List all collections in the catalog (paginated): name (the path through collection sets that the collection tools take), is_smart and photo_count.

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description: Create a collection; returns its path.

parent.description: Parent collection set path (optional), levels separated by ' / ' as in list_collections (e.g. 'Trips / 2026'). Missing sets are created; existing ones are reused, matching names ignoring case as Lightroom does. Omit it for a top-level collection; an empty level or a level with leading or trailing spaces or slashes is rejected.

tools.name: create_smart_collection
tools.description: Save intersecting search_photos filters as an auto-updating smart collection; at least one filter. Creates missing parent sets; rejects existing sibling names. Returns its path. Rules: give at least one search filter; start_date and end_date must be real calendar dates; start_date must be on or before end_date.

parent.description: Parent collection set path, with levels separated by ' / ' (e.g. 'Trips / 2026')

camera.description: Exact camera name indexed by Lightroom

lens.description: Exact lens name indexed by Lightroom

focal_length.description: Exact focal length in millimeters (not the 35mm equivalent)

edited.description: Whether the photo has develop adjustments

file_type.description: Lightroom file format; camera raw formats use RAW

folder.description: Folder text, including parent folders shown in Lightroom's Folders panel (contains all words)

tools.name: add_to_collection
tools.description: Add photos to a regular collection; a smart collection is refused. Returns added (the photos that were not members and are now) and already_in_collection (ids of photos that were members already, left as they were); unknown IDs are not_found.

collection_name.description: Collection path from list_collections, or a bare name. A listed path always picks that collection; a bare name of a nested collection must be unique.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

tools.name: get_collection_photos
tools.description: List the photos in a collection, regular or smart (paginated). Use a path from list_collections when names repeat; an ambiguous bare name is rejected.

include_path.description: Include each photo file path (default false). Rows always include photo_id, filename, rating (0 = unrated), flag, color_label and date_time_original, and stack (position, is_collapsed, top_photo_id) for a stacked photo.

collection_name.description: Collection path from list_collections, or a bare name. A listed path always picks that collection; a bare name of a nested collection must be unique.

tools.name: remove_from_collection
tools.description: Remove photos from a regular collection; catalog and other memberships stay. Returns removed (unique members) and not_in_collection (photo_ids that were not members); unknown IDs are not_found.

collection_name.description: Collection path from list_collections, or a bare name. A listed path always picks that collection; a bare name of a nested collection must be unique.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

tools.name: delete_collection
tools.description: Delete a collection; photos stay in the catalog. Returns photo_count, the photos it held.

collection_name.description: Collection path from list_collections, or a bare name. A listed path always picks that collection; a bare name of a nested collection must be unique.

tools.name: set_keywords
tools.description: Add/remove keyword names or parent-first '|' paths from list_keywords, ignoring case. Missing names create top-level keywords; paths create missing levels unless create_missing=false. Returns updated (photos written); unknown IDs are not_found; a call matching no photo creates no keyword. Rules: give add_keywords or remove_keywords.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

add_keywords.description: Keywords to add: plain names or 'Parent|Child' hierarchy paths

remove_keywords.description: Keywords to remove: a plain name removes every keyword with that name, a 'Parent|Child' path removes only that one

create_missing.description: Default true. When false, nothing is created: every keyword to add must already exist, a plain name must match exactly one keyword anywhere in the hierarchy, and the call fails without changing anything if any keyword is unknown or ambiguous.

tools.name: remove_keyword_subtree
tools.description: Detach a parent keyword and every descendant from photo_ids, or all tagged photos with catalog_wide=true. Matches paths ignoring case; unknown parent fails unchanged. Preserves unrelated and same-named keywords elsewhere. Keyword nodes stay in the catalog and list_keywords. Use a dedicated parent such as 'AI Keywords' with set_keywords to undo a tagging batch. Returns updated (photos changed) and removed (keyword assignments removed); unknown IDs are not_found. Rules: give photo_ids or catalog_wide true, not both.

parent.description: Parent-first keyword path, for example 'AI Keywords' or 'Tags|AI Keywords'

photo_ids.description: Photos to detach the subtree from; omit when catalog_wide is true

catalog_wide.description: Explicitly detach the subtree from every photo in the catalog; cannot accompany photo_ids

tools.name: list_keywords
tools.description: List paginated parent-first keyword paths ('Places|Europe|Paris'), synonyms and include_on_export (paginated). Pass paths to set_keywords; narrow large trees with parent/query or request paths_only.

parent.description: Only list keywords below this keyword path (optional)

query.description: Only list keywords whose name or a synonym contains this text, ignoring case (optional)

paths_only.description: Return each keyword as just its path string instead of an object (default false)

tools.name: rename_keyword
tools.description: Rename in place; tagged photos update, parent/children/synonyms stay. Case-insensitive sibling conflicts fail; case-only renames work. Returns old_path, new_path and photo_count.

keyword.description: Keyword from list_keywords: a unique plain name or a 'Parent|Child' path

new_name.description: New name for that keyword (a single name, not a path: no '|')

tools.name: undo_last_step
tools.description: Undo one shared Lightroom history step (confirm:true), including a user/other plug-in action after your edit. Ownership is unknown: call only if undoing the current last step is acceptable. Lightroom can merge recent plug-in writes, even across photos, into one step. Returns undone, can_undo and message.

confirm.description: Accept undoing the latest step in Lightroom's shared history

tools.name: set_rating_and_flag
tools.description: Set rating, flag, or both in one write. Returns updated (photos written); unknown IDs are not_found; get_photo_metadata and photo rows report rating (0 = unrated) and flag in the same values. Rules: give rating or flag.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

rating.description: Star rating (0-5); supply rating, flag, or both

tools.name: set_color_label
tools.description: Set a color label or none to clear; get_photo_metadata and photo rows report color_label in the same values; an unlabelled photo reads none. Returns updated (photos written); unknown IDs are not_found.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths

label.description: Color name, or none to clear the label

tools.name: remove_photos_from_catalog
tools.description: Remove up to 100 IDs/paths from catalog, losing catalog edits/metadata; files remain on disk (confirm:true). Include every virtual copy with its master; a photo in a collapsed stack is refused until the stack is expanded in Lightroom; a path shared with copies is refused; use numeric IDs. Deduplicates; returns removed; unknown IDs are not_found. Opens Library grid on the photos' folders (else All Photographs), restores module/sources/surviving selection; Library stays in grid view.

photo_ids.description: Photo IDs or file paths to remove from the catalog

confirm.description: Explicit consent to lose these photos' catalog edits and metadata

tools.name: import_photos
tools.description: Import a photo or a folder recursively. A JPEG with a non-DNG raw file of exactly the same name (only the extension's case may differ) stays the raw's sidecar: folders leave it out and report skipped_sidecar_jpegs; importing that JPEG alone fails and names the raw. Other JPEGs import as their own photos. Files already in the catalog are left unchanged and counted in already_in_catalog. A file whose folder, or whose name within its folder, differs only in case from one in the catalog fails, because Lightroom matches both case-insensitively; on a case-insensitive volume such a name is the same file and counts in already_in_catalog. Lightroom and Photos library packages are skipped. Returns imported, already_in_catalog, added_to_collection, skipped_by_extension, skipped_sidecar_jpegs and skipped_package_files; a file that fails is failed {path, reason} when nothing was written for it (a busy catalog included) and unknown when something was, naming it (a copy or folder copy_to made, or the photo addPhoto may have added); a single-file source raises instead, with the same class; files not reached before the time budget are remaining; photos not added to the collection make the result partial. A failed file leaves the catalog and disk unchanged.

source_path.description: Absolute path of the photo or folder to import; ~/ is expanded; only the platform's separator between names (/ on macOS, \ on Windows); no ., .. or empty names. Folder imports accept camera raw (CR3, RAF, ORF, RW2, NEF, ARW, DNG and other Camera Raw formats), JPEG, HEIC/HEIF, AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF, PNG and PSD/PSB; other files are skipped by extension.

collection_name.description: Collection path from list_collections, or a bare name. A listed path always picks that collection; a bare name of a nested collection must be unique. Imported and already cataloged photos are added to it; an unknown or smart collection fails before importing (optional).

copy_to.description: Absolute path of a folder to copy files and sidecars into, keeping subfolders, and import the copies; ~/ is expanded; only the platform's separator between names (/ on macOS, \ on Windows); no ., .. or empty names (optional)

separate_jpegs.description: Also add a JPEG that would stay a raw file's sidecar as its own photo (default false)

tools.name: export_photos
tools.description: Export photos, optionally with a saved export preset; format/quality/width/height override only those preset settings. Skips the preset's collision prompt and after-export action. While get_photo_detail or another export runs, the call is refused, not queued: failed with nothing exported; call again once it finishes. A photo with outdated AI settings can open Lightroom's AI Updates dialog, which blocks until dismissed. Returns written files {photo_id, path}, skipped photo_ids (on_existing skip), destination and preset; a photo whose export failed before its session started is failed, and one whose session failed after it started (Cancel in "AI Updates Recommended" included) is unknown, naming the export and what it leaves on the photo (one Export history step and the exported mark); both keep the files already written; photos not reached before the time budget are remaining. Argument and overwrite refusals change nothing. Rules: give destination or export_preset; export_preset_folder needs export_preset.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths to export

destination.description: Absolute path of the export folder, created if missing; ~/ is expanded; only the platform's separator between names (/ on macOS, \ on Windows); no ., .. or empty names, no control characters. Optional if export_preset has a fixed destination

export_preset.description: Export preset title, file name, id or file path (list_export_presets)

quality.description: JPEG quality (0-100), default 90; with a preset it overrides the preset's quality and turns off its file size limit

on_existing.description: What to do when the destination already holds a file with that name (default rename). Lightroom never prompts. overwrite is refused into any catalog folder.

tools.name: list_export_presets
tools.description: List saved export presets (not Lightroom's built-ins) with folder, file, id, format, quality, size, file_naming and destination. Only usable: true (Hard Drive) presets work with export_photos; others give unusable_reason.

tools.name: export_photo_metadata
tools.description: Export up to 1000 photos to disk JSON: file/capture time/dimensions/rating/flag/color_label/title/caption/GPS/location/keywords/keyword_paths (version 2 file, snake_case keys, string photo_id), no develop settings. Omitted photo_ids uses selection, or filmstrip if none. Prefer over per-photo get_photo_metadata. Returns exported count and destination; unknown IDs are not_found.

photo_ids.description: Array of photo IDs or file paths (default: current selection)

destination.description: Absolute path of the .json file to write; ~/ is expanded; only the platform's separator between names (/ on macOS, \ on Windows); no ., .. or empty names

overwrite.description: Replace the file if it already exists (default false: fail instead)

instructions:
Every tool answers with JSON {outcome, data, error, failed, unknown, not_found, remaining, warnings}. outcome done means everything asked for happened and was confirmed, and only then is isError unset. partial: data holds what happened, the lists say what did not. failed: nothing changed: the call wrote nothing, or every write it made was read back as undone (Lightroom's undo history can still hold such a write and its restore as steps). unknown: something may have changed, and the error names what Lightroom reported written (a reply lost in transit carries only its error); read the current state before retrying. The class comes from what the call wrote, not from the kind of error. failed items are safe to retry once their reason is fixed, unknown items need a read first, not_found lists inputs the catalog does not have, and remaining lists inputs not finished: resend exactly those; a preview batch may list the item it was fetching, and previews are read-only and safe to resend. warnings never change the outcome.

Photo ids the catalog resolved are strings in every reply, while not_found and remaining echo the inputs as given; an input names a photo by its id (a number or digit string) or by an absolute file path. get_develop_settings is the one develop read, by the SDK names set_develop_settings writes. Each develop key's kind and range are in the set_develop_settings schema, and the rules between keys (crop edges, Defringe hue pairs, Glow style, GrayMixer needing black and white) are checked against the stored values before writing; a refused write changes nothing. Lightroom normalises a write within about a second, so develop writes read the values back then: a value stored differently is listed in adjusted and the outcome is partial. describe_develop_keys reports Lightroom's own ranges for a photo. Read the current crop with get_crop and set a frame as the photo is displayed, or inside the current crop, with set_crop; switch colour or black and white with set_treatment. Judge sharpness on get_photo_detail's 1:1 crops of a full render; previews show the whole frame scaled down. search_photos does not see the hidden photos of a collapsed stack, and a warning names the stack tops on the page.

Calls that drive Develop, write develop settings or read a photo's develop settings, masks or snapshots run one at a time in arrival order, across every client of this server (get_photo_detail's first step reads the cropped frame this way, then renders alongside them); a call waits for the ones before it within its own time budget and fails without effect if its turn does not come: call again once the Develop call before it has answered. Catalog reads, other catalog writes, previews and exports run alongside them. A call that timed out is asked to stop and keeps the turn until Lightroom has finished it or 60 s have passed since the timeout; a call still running after that can overlap the next one, and its outcome stays unknown. This includes Denoise, Remove spots, Develop adjustments, develop settings, presets, snapshots, undo and mask calls, including People and Landscape computation. Every catalog write waits up to 10 s while Lightroom or another plug-in is writing; if the catalog stays busy, a call that had written nothing is failed, and one that had is unknown and names what it wrote.

Tools that open a photo in Develop restore the user's module, view source and selection afterwards, and a warning names anything they could not restore; invert_mask's copy restores the masking tool and the selected mask. invert_mask opens the named photo in Develop and reads Develop's mask list: it waits up to 5 seconds until Lightroom lists the masks its saved settings hold; while it lists fewer masks than the saved settings hold (Develop has not loaded them yet, or an alert from the user's own work in Lightroom, such as "No sky detected", is open), the call is failed with nothing changed: click OK in Lightroom if an alert is open, then call again. Unknown mask ids fail without changing the photo. A new geometry mask created without adjustments, and every new People and Landscape mask, adjusts nothing until set_mask_adjustments is called; on a raw the write itself can re-render fine texture, so compare regional means, not pixels.

Guarded mask writes (create_gradient_mask, update_gradient_mask, create_brush_mask, add_brush_strokes, create_range_mask, create_mask, create_mask_batch, combine_mask, and a full copy_develop_settings when the source has masks to copy or the target has masks to remove) run on the live kit's throwaway catalog, and elsewhere only after a certification run on this machine passed for the running Lightroom version and build and the photo's process version; get_mask_write_admission reports this without writing. They use Lightroom's undocumented develop-setting format: check what they construct or change against the format certification tested, leave every other mask as Lightroom stored it, read back the full mask list (a mask they left alone must come back exactly), and roll back to the previous masks on mismatch. Uncertified versions or a constructed mask outside the tested format fail unchanged. AI masks a call writes (create_mask, create_mask_batch, combine_mask's component, a full copy_develop_settings) or a preset adds are judged on the photo after one Update AI Settings: the call's own masks are the ones it wrote (for a preset, the entries that were not on the photo before); a photo where anything is still computing 15 s later is unknown and nothing more is written to it; an own mask Lightroom could not compute restores the previous masks and fails, or is unknown when the restore cannot be confirmed or the recompute changed other develop settings (a preset keeps its masks and is unknown); an existing AI mask whose result the photo-wide recompute changed, or one already failed before the call, is named in a warning. A full copy_develop_settings decides admission, a target mask Lightroom has not named yet and the format of the copied masks before its first write to a target: a refusal decided before writing leaves the target unchanged; an unknown item names what was written: read the target.

Positions for gradient, brush and range masks are normalized 0 to 1 in the frame of the rendered preview, as get_photo_preview shows it: after the develop crop, straighten and displayed orientation, origin top-left, y increasing down. The tools convert them to the frame Lightroom stores and answer in the preview frame. Lightroom stores masks before the crop, so a mask stays on the same part of the photo when the crop changes later. Out-of-range positions fail before writing. Gradient widths and heights are fractions of the preview width and height, measured before rotation; rotation is clockwise. Brush radius is a fraction of the preview's longer edge. Lightroom also draws masks through Upright, Transform and manual distortion, which have no inverse: with one of them active the write is made with a warning that a position can land up to about 0.05 of the frame away near the edges; check the render.

Mask slider writes and mask creation use the local_* SDK names; each slider's range is in the schema, and describe_develop_keys with mask_id reports where Lightroom's live range differs. Unknown sliders or out-of-range values fail before writing. set_mask_adjustments, set_mask_curves, edit_mask_point_colors and get_mask work on the photo's saved settings by mask_id, without opening Develop or selecting the mask. A write changes only the named sliders, channels or swatches (sliders are stored to six decimal places and colour-grade sliders as whole numbers, a curve takes at most 16 points and a linear curve is stored as no curve, Point Color values keep six decimals; the reply gives the stored values), turns the mask on as Lightroom's own sliders do (a mask list_masks shows as hidden is shown again, and a warning says so), adds one history step and is read back exactly (a request that changes no stored value writes nothing); if Lightroom changed anything else, or stored another value, the photo is put back (one more history step) and the call fails naming what Lightroom stored; if the restore cannot be confirmed either, the call is unknown. Slider changes the person has pending in Develop are committed before a call reads or writes anything, so a read shows them and a write builds on them. These edits preserve other masks and global settings.
